intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Temple Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent 12th-century Khmer temple complex at sunrise, wandering through Angkor Wat, Bayon, and Ta Prohm. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a full-day small circuit tour covering the most iconic temples with rich historical context.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine white-sand beaches of Koh Rong Samloem island. Spend the day snorkeling in crystal-clear turquoise waters, relaxing on Saracen Bay, and exploring the unspoiled jungle interior. One of Southeast Asia's most beautiful and tranquil island beaches.
experiences.location: Saracen Bay, Koh Rong Samloem Island

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda Visit
experiences.description: Tour the stunning Royal Palace complex and the adjacent Silver Pagoda, home to a floor of 5,000 silver tiles and a life-sized gold Buddha adorned with diamonds. Gain deep insight into Cambodian royal culture, Buddhist traditions, and Khmer architecture spanning centuries.

experiences.name: Khmer Cooking Class with Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Khmer cooking class beginning with a guided tour of a local wet market to select fresh ingredients. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and Mango Salad. Includes a sit-down meal of everything you cook and a recipe booklet to take home.

experiences.name: Tonle Sap Floating Village Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the remarkable floating villages of Kampong Phluk on Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Witness entire communities — schools, temples, and homes — built on stilts or floating platforms. Learn about the unique aquatic lifestyle of Cambodian fishing communities and observe local daily life up close.
experiences.location: Kampong Phluk, Tonle Sap Lake, Siem Reap Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at airport, clear immigration and collect luggage. Take a budget tuk-tuk (~$5–7) to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll around the guesthouse neighborhood to get your bearings. Visit the nearby Angkor National Museum entrance area (exterior view, save museum entry for another day) and pick up a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62) from the official ticket office before it closes at 17:30 — this is essential for the coming days.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Siem Reap's Old Market (Phsar Chas) area by tuk-tuk (~$2–3). Explore the vibrant Pub Street and the surrounding night market stalls. Enjoy a relaxed first evening soaking in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal or airport snack
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap meal at the airport or a local roadside stall near your guesthouse ($2–4)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Khmer restaurant near Old Market — try 'Khmer Kitchen Restaurant' or 'Dakshin' for authentic local dishes like Amok fish curry and rice for $4–7 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Angkor Pass on arrival day — it's valid for 3 days within 7 days and the ticket office closes at 17:30. Confirm your tuk-tuk driver's contact; hiring a regular driver for the week ($10–15/day) saves money. November is the tail end of rainy season — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn (4:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise — one of the most spectacular sights in Southeast Asia. Arrive at the main reflecting pool by 5:15 AM. After sunrise, explore the vast Angkor Wat temple complex (included in your Angkor Pass) — spend 2–3 hours walking through the galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or hire your tuk-tuk to nearby Angkor Thom complex. Visit the Bayon Temple with its famous 216 serene stone faces, then explore the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Rest during the hottest hours (12:00–14:00) under shade or at a nearby food stall.
day_by_day.evening: Return to guesthouse to rest and shower. Head to Siem Reap's Night Market or Angkor Night Market for budget souvenir shopping and street food browsing. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance if budget allows ($12–15 with dinner show) or watch free performances at some local restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and water the night before for the early sunrise — bananas, bread, and bottled water from a local convenience store ($1–2)
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the local food stalls just outside the Angkor Thom complex — rice with grilled pork or noodle soup for $2–3
meals.dinner: Street food at Angkor Night Market or a local Khmer restaurant — try 'Chanrey Tree' for affordable Khmer cuisine ($5–8 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start extremely early for sunrise — bring a flashlight/phone torch and insect repellent. Stay hydrated; temple walking in the heat is exhausting. Dress respectfully (shoulders and knees covered) for all temple visits. Your Angkor Pass Day 1 of 3 used today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm temple (the 'Tomb Raider' temple) early morning when crowds are thinner. Marvel at the massive strangler fig and silk-cotton trees growing through and around the ancient stone structures. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring its atmospheric jungle-entwined ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Banteay Kdei and the nearby Srah Srang reservoir (a beautiful royal bathing pool) — both are peaceful and less crowded. Then visit Pre Rup temple, an impressive 10th-century state temple with great views from its upper tiers. Head back to your guesthouse for a mid-afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local Khmer village near your guesthouse on foot or by bicycle (many guesthouses rent bicycles for $2–3/day). Visit a local pagoda (wat) at dusk when monks return for evening prayers — a peaceful and culturally rich experience. Stroll back for a quiet evening meal.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or a nearby local café — Khmer rice porridge (bobor) or baguette with eggs for $1.50–3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stall near the temples — fried rice or noodles for $2–3
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local family-run restaurant near your accommodation — try fish amok or lok lak (stir-fried beef) with rice for $4–6

day_by_day.notes: Angkor Pass Day 2 of 3 used today. Rent a bicycle for a more immersive and budget-friendly way to explore the smaller temple loop. Carry at least 1.5 liters of water per person.

day_by_day.morning: Use your final Angkor Pass day to visit the remote and less-touristed temples: Banteay Srei — a stunning 10th-century temple dedicated to Shiva, famous for its intricate pink sandstone carvings. It's about 25 km from Siem Reap — hire your tuk-tuk driver (~$15 round trip). Arrive early for the best light and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at the Landmine Museum (donation-based entry, ~$5 suggested) — a sobering and important cultural experience that tells the story of Cambodia's tragic recent history and ongoing demining efforts. Then visit the Cambodia Landmine Relief Fund's craft shop to support survivors.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, visit the vibrant Phsar Chas (Old Market) for last-minute browsing. Enjoy a traditional Khmer cooking class if budget allows ($15–25) or simply enjoy a relaxed evening meal and reflect on the temple experiences of the past three days.

meals.breakfast: Local café breakfast — French baguette with pâté (a colonial legacy) and iced coffee for $2–3
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the Banteay Srei trip or eat at a local restaurant in the area for $3–4
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer Khmer dinner — 'Mahob Restaurant' or 'Cuisine Wat Damnak' (if budget stretches) for $8–15, or keep it budget with a street food spread at Old Market

day_by_day.notes: Angkor Pass Day 3 of 3 used today — all three days of your pass are now fully utilized. Book transport to Phnom Penh for tomorrow (bus is the most budget-friendly option — Giant Ibis or Mekong Express, ~$12–15, departs around 7:00–8:00 AM). Book tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up and check out of your Siem Reap guesthouse. Board your budget bus to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours, $12–15 with a reputable company like Giant Ibis). Enjoy the Cambodian countryside scenery en route. Arrive in Phnom Penh around 13:00–14:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a budget guesthouse in Phnom Penh (BKK1 or Riverside area recommended, $8–18/night for a clean dorm or private room). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (entry ~$10) — a stunning complex of Khmer royal architecture with gilded spires, the sacred Emerald Buddha, and a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Tonle Sap and Mekong Riverside promenade as the sun sets — a lively and scenic area with locals exercising, families picnicking, and street vendors. Browse the Riverside Night Market for local snacks and crafts.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure — local bread stall or guesthouse breakfast for $1.50–2.50
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus or at a roadside stop en route ($2–4)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Khmer restaurant near the Riverside — try 'Friends Restaurant' (a social enterprise supporting at-risk youth) for $5–10 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book your Phnom Penh accommodation in advance. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety and reliability. Keep your valuables secure in Phnom Penh — bag snatching can occur near the riverside. Store your large luggage at the guesthouse.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison, entry $8) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison that now serves as a powerful and deeply moving memorial to the victims of the genocide (1975–1979). Allow 2–3 hours. This is a sobering but essential cultural and historical experience for understanding modern Cambodia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk (~$5–8) to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields, entry $6 including audio guide) — located about 15 km south of the city. The audio guide is excellent and tells personal survivor stories. Pay respects at the memorial stupa containing the remains of victims. Return to the city center by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — an Art Deco landmark with a distinctive yellow dome. Browse stalls selling jewelry, clothing, and local goods. Enjoy a street food dinner at the nearby stalls or visit the Russian Market area for a more local experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery or café near your guesthouse — coffee and pastry or rice porridge for $2–3
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Tuol Sleng — local noodle soup or rice dish at a nearby eatery for $2–4
meals.dinner: Street food dinner near Central Market — grilled corn, baguette sandwiches, and fresh fruit for $3–5, or sit-down Khmer meal for $5–7

day_by_day.notes: The Killing Fields and S-21 are emotionally heavy experiences — allow yourself time to process. The audio guide at Choeung Ek is highly recommended and included in the entry fee. Dress respectfully (no shorts or sleeveless tops). Take breaks as needed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia (entry $10) — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture, including pre-Angkorian pieces dating back to the 4th century. Spend 2 hours exploring the beautiful terracotta-roofed building and its tranquil courtyard garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the BKK1 neighborhood on foot — a trendy area with independent cafés, boutique shops, and NGO-run social enterprise restaurants. Visit the Wat Phnom hill temple (entry $1) — the spiritual heart of Phnom Penh, a small but charming hilltop pagoda with resident monkeys. Then prepare for your onward journey: book a night bus or early morning bus to Sihanoukville/Kampot for the beach portion of your trip.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your last evening in Phnom Penh with a sunset cruise on the Mekong River (budget options from $5–8 per person) or simply watch the sunset from the riverside promenade. Pack your bags for the morning departure.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at 'The Blue Pumpkin' or a local café — smoothie bowl or eggs and toast for $3–5
meals.lunch: Lunch at a social enterprise restaurant — 'Romdeng' (traditional Khmer food, supports street children) for $6–10
meals.dinner: Farewell Phnom Penh dinner — Khmer BBQ (local-style grilled meats and seafood) at a riverside restaurant for $6–10 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book your transport to Kampot or Sihanoukville tonight — buses depart early morning (~7:00 AM). Kampot is recommended for a more relaxed, budget-friendly beach-adjacent experience. Giant Ibis or Mekong Express to Kampot costs ~$9–12 and takes ~3.5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Early bus from Phnom Penh to Kampot (departs ~7:00 AM, arrives ~10:30–11:00 AM, ~$9–12). Arrive in the charming riverside colonial town of Kampot. Check into a budget guesthouse or riverside hostel ($8–15/night). Rent a bicycle ($2–3/day) or motorbike ($6–8/day) and explore the sleepy, picturesque Old Town with its French colonial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or ride to the nearby Bokor National Park road for scenic views, or head to one of the local pepper plantations for a free or low-cost guided tour — Kampot pepper is world-famous and the farms are fascinating. Alternatively, visit the cave temples at Phnom Chhnork (entry ~$1) — a beautiful natural cave with a 5th-century brick temple inside.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot town for a relaxed riverside evening. The Kampot waterfront is perfect for a sunset stroll. Enjoy the laid-back backpacker-meets-local atmosphere at one of the riverside bars or restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Snack on the bus or eat at the Phnom Penh bus station before departure ($1–2)
meals.lunch: Late lunch upon arrival in Kampot — local noodle soup or Khmer curry at a riverside eatery for $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant in Kampot — try fresh Kampot pepper crab or grilled fish for $5–9 per person at a local spot

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is one of Cambodia's most charming and budget-friendly destinations. November weather should be pleasant — dry season is beginning. The town is very walkable and bicycle-friendly. Be cautious when renting motorbikes — check the condition before accepting.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kep — a small, elegant seaside town 25 km from Kampot (tuk-tuk ~$8–10 round trip or motorbike rental). Visit the famous Kep Crab Market — a string of wooden seafood restaurants on stilts over the water, serving the freshest and most affordable crab in Cambodia (Kampot pepper crab is a must-try, ~$8–12 per dish). Walk through the atmospheric ruins of abandoned French colonial villas that line the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Kep Beach or take a short boat ride (~$5–8 return) to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a pristine, low-key island with clear water, white sand, and basic beach bungalows. Swim, snorkel, and relax on the beach. Return to Kep or Kampot by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot for your final evening. Join a sunset kayaking tour on the Kampot River through the mangroves (~$8–12 per person) — a magical experience as fireflies begin to appear at dusk. Enjoy a final Kampot dinner at a riverside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Kampot guesthouse or a local café — eggs, toast, and coffee for $2–4
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kep Crab Market — fresh Kampot pepper crab or grilled squid with rice for $8–12 (a worthwhile splurge)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Kampot — grilled fish or amok curry at a riverside restaurant for $5–8 per person, with a local Angkor beer ($1)

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island boats typically run until 15:00–16:00 — don't miss the last boat back. Kep Crab Market is the highlight of this region — budget accordingly for a slightly more expensive but unforgettable lunch. The firefly kayaking in Kampot is one of Cambodia's hidden gems.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cambodia — enjoy a slow breakfast in Kampot. If time permits before departure, take a final cycle around the Old Town, visit the local morning market (Phsar Kandal) to pick up last-minute souvenirs like Kampot pepper, palm sugar, or locally made crafts at very reasonable prices. Reflect on the incredible journey through Cambodia's history, culture, and natural beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange transport back to Phnom Penh airport or Sihanoukville depending on your departure flight (bus ~$9–12, ~3.5 hours to Phnom Penh). Allow plenty of time for travel — aim to arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight. Complete any last-minute shopping at the airport or en route.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia. Reflect on 10 incredible days exploring the temples of Angkor, the history of Phnom Penh, and the relaxed coastal charm of Kampot and Kep.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — rice porridge with ginger and chicken (borbor) or French baguette with local pâté for $2–3 at a Kampot café
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a roadside stop en route to the airport or at the airport ($3–6)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 10 days: Accommodation ($80–150), Transport ($60–90), Food ($100–150), Angkor Pass ($62), Museum entries ($30–40), Activities ($30–50) — Total approximately $360–540 USD for a comfortable budget trip. Exchange leftover Cambodian Riel before departure as it is not widely exchangeable abroad. USD is widely accepted throughout Cambodia.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel near Angkor Archaeological Park. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around the hotel neighborhood. Visit the nearby Angkor Wat outer wall and reflection pond for a first iconic glimpse — no entry ticket needed for the exterior view. Pick up a multi-day Angkor Pass at the official ticket office (1-day or 3-day pass recommended).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area in Siem Reap town for a lively introduction to local street life, souvenir browsing, and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Inflight or at airport — skip or grab a snack on arrival
meals.lunch: Light meal at a café near the airport or hotel upon arrival — try 'The Sugar Palm' or a local noodle shop (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Mahob Restaurant' or 'Cuisine Wat Damnak' for authentic Khmer cuisine in a mid-range setting (~$12–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Angkor Archaeological Park pass today to save time tomorrow morning. Passes are sold until 17:30. Keep hydrated — November is warm but manageable (~28°C).

day_by_day.morning: Early sunrise visit to Angkor Wat (arrive by 05:30 for the iconic sunrise reflection). Explore the main temple complex — the five towers, bas-relief galleries depicting Hindu epics, and the inner sanctum. Hire a licensed local guide at the gate (~$25–30) for rich historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Angkor Thom complex: enter via the South Gate with its stone face towers, explore the Bayon Temple (famous for 216 serene stone faces), the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Take a tuk-tuk between sites (~$15–20 for the day).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap for dinner, then attend an Apsara dance performance — a UNESCO-recognized classical Khmer dance tradition. 'Angkor Village Theatre' or 'Smile of Angkor' offer dinner-show packages.

meals.breakfast: Early snack or coffee from a vendor near Angkor Wat gate, or pre-pack from hotel (~$2–4)
meals.lunch: Local Khmer restaurant near Angkor Thom — try 'Angkor Café' or a roadside stall for amok fish curry and rice (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner-and-show package at Apsara performance venue (~$18–25 per person including show)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and light, breathable clothing. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) to enter temple sanctuaries. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ta Prohm — the atmospheric 'jungle temple' famously left partially unrestored with giant tree roots engulfing the stone walls (made famous by the film Tomb Raider). Arrive early to beat tour groups. Then visit Banteay Kdei and the sacred Srah Srang reservoir for peaceful reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive (~30 min by tuk-tuk) to Banteay Srei, the 'Citadel of Women' — a 10th-century temple renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest in all of Angkor. Visit the nearby Angkor National Museum back in town for deeper historical and cultural context (~$12 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique — watch silk weavers and wood carvers preserving traditional Khmer crafts. Stroll the Night Market for local handicrafts and gifts.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel or a nearby café — try a Khmer baguette sandwich (French-influenced local staple) (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or local eatery near Banteay Srei — simple Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) (~$3–6)
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Malis Restaurant' — upscale Khmer cuisine in a garden setting, known for traditional recipes (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is about 25 km from Angkor Wat — confirm tuk-tuk fare in advance (~$20–25 round trip). The Angkor National Museum closes at 18:30.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Preah Khan — a vast, largely unrestored temple complex with long atmospheric corridors, jungle vegetation, and intricate carvings. Then explore Neak Pean, an artificial island temple set in a large baray (reservoir), and Ta Som, a small but beautifully intimate temple with a famous tree-covered east gopura.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the West Baray — a massive ancient reservoir still used for swimming and boating by locals. Rent a boat to reach the West Mebon island temple ruins in the center. Enjoy the peaceful, off-the-beaten-path atmosphere away from main tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class experience in Siem Reap — learn to prepare 3–4 traditional Khmer dishes including fish amok, green mango salad, and lok lak. 'Le Tigre de Papier' and 'Cooks in Tuk Tuks' offer excellent mid-range classes (~$25–35 per person).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — Khmer rice porridge (babor) with ginger and herbs (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style or local vendor near West Baray — fresh coconut, grilled corn, and local snacks (~$4–6)
meals.dinner: Your own cooking class creations — a delicious and memorable meal included in the class price

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class dinner counts as your evening meal — book in advance as classes fill up. West Baray is best visited in the afternoon when light is softer.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Phnom Kulen National Park (~50 km from Siem Reap, ~1.5 hr drive). Hike through the jungle to the sacred Kbal Spean 'River of a Thousand Lingas' — a riverbed carved with thousands of Hindu symbols and mythological figures. A deeply spiritual and historically significant site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Phnom Kulen to see the giant reclining Buddha carved into a sandstone boulder, and swim in the refreshing waterfall pools — a favorite with locals. Explore the remnants of the ancient Mahendraparvata city, considered the birthplace of the Khmer Empire.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap by early evening. Rest and recover, then enjoy a traditional Khmer massage at one of the town's reputable spas (~$12–18/hour). Try 'Frangipani Spa' or 'Bodia Spa'.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or eat at a local stall near Phnom Kulen entrance — grilled meats, sticky rice, and fruit (~$5–7)
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at 'Viroth's Restaurant' — elegant Khmer dishes in a stylish courtyard setting (~$12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Kulen has a separate entry fee (~$20/person). Hire a private car or join a guided day tour (~$35–50 total) as the road can be rough. Wear sturdy shoes for the hike.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: depart Siem Reap by bus or private taxi to Phnom Penh (~6 hours by road, or 45-min domestic flight). Giant Ibis or Mekong Express buses are comfortable and mid-range (~$15–20). If flying, book in advance (~$50–80). Depart by 07:00 to arrive by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Phnom Penh accommodation. Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring stunning Khmer architecture, the Throne Hall, and the Silver Pagoda with its floor of 5,000 silver tiles and a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with 9,584 diamonds.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade — the heart of Phnom Penh's social life. Watch the sunset over the Tonle Sap and Mekong river confluence. Browse the riverfront bars and restaurants for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure — hotel or local bakery (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Onboard snack on bus, or stop at a roadside restaurant en route (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Romdeng' — a social enterprise restaurant serving traditional Cambodian cuisine, located in a French colonial villa (~$12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance during peak season. The Royal Palace closes at 11:00–14:00 for lunch — plan your afternoon visit accordingly. Entry fee ~$10 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply sobering but essential historical site documenting the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). Hire an audio guide or a survivor guide for a powerful and respectful experience. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Killing Fields of Choeung Ek (~15 km from city center) — the most significant memorial site of the genocide, with a Buddhist stupa containing victims' remains. The audio guide (included in entry) is exceptionally well-produced. Take time to reflect. Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia for ancient Khmer art and sculpture collections.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Phnom Penh Night Market and Central Market (Phsar Thmei) dome area. Enjoy a lighter, reflective evening after an emotionally heavy day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near your accommodation (~$4–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the National Museum — 'Friends the Restaurant' (social enterprise training vulnerable youth) is excellent (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Topaz Restaurant' or 'Khmer Surin' — quality Khmer and Thai-Khmer fusion in a relaxed atmosphere (~$12–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek are emotionally intense — allow yourself time to process. These sites are critical to understanding Cambodian history and culture. Dress respectfully and speak quietly.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: depart Phnom Penh for Sihanoukville (~4 hours by bus or taxi) or take a direct bus/ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island (~5–6 hours total). Giant Ibis or GTVC buses to Sihanoukville depart regularly (~$10–15). From Sihanoukville, take a speed boat to the island (~$25–30 round trip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Samloem — one of Cambodia's most beautiful and relatively undeveloped islands. Check in to a mid-range beachside bungalow. Spend the afternoon swimming in the crystal-clear turquoise waters of Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay. Snorkel around the coral reefs.
day_by_day.evening: Witness the magical bioluminescent plankton in the shallow waters after dark — a natural phenomenon Koh Rong Samloem is famous for. Simply wade into the water and watch the blue-green glow around your hands and feet.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure from Phnom Penh (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus or eat at Sihanoukville port while waiting for the ferry (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood dinner at a beachside restaurant on Koh Rong Samloem — grilled fish, prawns, and rice with a sunset view (~$10–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets and island accommodation in advance. There are no ATMs on the island — bring sufficient cash. November weather is generally dry and ideal for beach activities.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day on Koh Rong Samloem. Morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding around the island's coastline. Explore the quieter northern beaches accessible by foot or kayak. Snorkeling equipment can be rented from most guesthouses (~$5/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day island boat tour to snorkel at multiple coral reef spots around the island, visit a secluded beach, and spot tropical fish. Tours typically run 13:00–17:00 (~$15–20 per person). Alternatively, hike the jungle trail across the island to the wild west beach for a dramatic contrast to the calm east side.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach. Join other travelers for a bonfire or beach gathering — the island has a relaxed social atmosphere. Stargaze from the beach with minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit platter and coffee at your guesthouse or a beachside café (~$4–6)
meals.lunch: Freshly caught grilled fish with rice and vegetables at a local beach shack (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Seafood BBQ on the beach — many restaurants offer daily catch BBQ platters with sides (~$12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Respect the island's fragile ecosystem — avoid touching coral, use reef-safe sunscreen, and do not litter. The island has limited electricity (often generator-powered evenings only) — embrace the off-grid experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the island — early swim or sunrise walk along the beach. Pack up and check out. Take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville, then arrange transport back to Phnom Penh airport or Siem Reap depending on your departure flight. Phnom Penh International Airport is ~4 hours from Sihanoukville by road.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time allows before departure, stop at a local market in Sihanoukville or Phnom Penh for last-minute souvenir shopping — silk scarves, Kampot pepper, Khmer art prints, and handmade jewelry make excellent gifts. Reflect on the journey over a final Khmer coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia. If your flight is in the evening, enjoy a final dinner at Phnom Penh airport or a nearby restaurant. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at island guesthouse before ferry departure (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sihanoukville or en route — local Khmer restaurant near the port (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Final dinner at Phnom Penh — 'Eleven One Kitchen' or airport restaurant for a relaxed last meal (~$10–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return transport and flight details the night before. Allow extra time for road traffic between Sihanoukville and Phnom Penh — it can be slow. Cambodian Riel and USD are both widely accepted; exchange any remaining Riel before departure as it is difficult to exchange abroad.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to boutique stay within Angkor Archaeological Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at the boutique property and settle in. Enjoy a welcome drink and orientation briefing with a dedicated concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel gardens to acclimate. Optional: light visit to the nearby Angkor Thom South Gate (just minutes away) for a gentle first glimpse of the ancient city without overexertion after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cocktails at the hotel terrace or rooftop overlooking the jungle canopy. Followed by a curated welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring modern Khmer cuisine with locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel upon arrival — fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian spring rolls, and iced jasmine tea
meals.dinner: In-house fine dining: Amok Trei (coconut fish curry in banana leaf), lok lak beef tenderloin, and mango sticky rice for dessert, paired with curated Cambodian craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in in advance if possible. Ensure passports and visas are in order. November weather in Siem Reap is ideal — dry season with temperatures around 28–32°C. Light linen clothing recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private guided tour of Angkor Wat at sunrise (depart hotel at 05:00). Experience the iconic reflection of the temple spires in the lotus pond with minimal crowds. Private Egyptologist-style Khmer historian guide explains the bas-reliefs and cosmological symbolism of the world's largest religious monument.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to hotel for a lavish champagne brunch. After rest, explore the Bayon Temple at Angkor Thom — famous for its 216 serene stone faces — and the Terrace of the Elephants and Terrace of the Leper King with your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Apsara dance performance dinner at a heritage venue near Siem Reap town. Traditional Khmer royal court dance performed by classically trained dancers, accompanied by a seven-course royal Khmer banquet.

meals.breakfast: Champagne brunch at the hotel: eggs benedict, fresh papaya, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), croissants, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and cold-pressed juices at the temple complex picnic prepared by the hotel
meals.dinner: Royal Khmer banquet at Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor or equivalent heritage venue — amuse-bouche, prawn bisque, grilled river fish, beef lok lak, and lotus seed dessert

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Angkor Wat by 05:30 for optimal sunrise positioning. Wear modest clothing covering shoulders and knees for temple entry. Bring insect repellent and sunscreen. Angkor Archaeological Park pass (3-day or 7-day) should be arranged by concierge in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Ta Prohm — the legendary 'Tomb Raider' temple where giant silk-cotton tree roots dramatically engulf the ancient stone ruins. Explore the atmospheric jungle temple in the cool morning hours with a specialist guide narrating the Jayavarman VII era history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Preah Khan Temple, a vast monastic complex with long atmospheric corridors and intricate carvings. Followed by a visit to the Angkor Conservation Centre (if accessible) or the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap town for deeper historical context with premium skip-the-line access.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class at a luxury villa in Siem Reap — learn to prepare three traditional Khmer dishes with a master chef, using ingredients sourced from the local Phsar Leu market. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel: French press coffee, eggs cooked to order, fresh tropical fruit platter, and Cambodian banana pancakes
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Cuisine Wat Damnak or equivalent — seasonal tasting menu featuring local Cambodian ingredients in contemporary presentation
meals.dinner: Khmer dishes prepared during cooking class: fish amok, green mango salad, and banana blossom curry, served with jasmine rice and palm sugar dessert

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm is best visited early to avoid tour groups. The cooking class can be customized to dietary requirements — inform the concierge 24 hours ahead. Angkor National Museum tickets should be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private hot air balloon flight over the Angkor Archaeological Park (weather permitting) — witness the temple complex from above at golden hour. Alternatively, a private helicopter scenic flight over Angkor Wat and the surrounding jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the remote and exquisitely carved Banteay Srei Temple — the 'Citadel of Women' — renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in all of Angkor. Accompanied by a senior Khmer art historian guide. En route, stop at the landmine museum for a sobering and important cultural education.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Siem Reap town (FCC Angkor or equivalent). Followed by dinner at a premium restaurant on Pub Street's refined end or a private riverside dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-flight breakfast at the hotel: granola, yogurt, tropical fruits, and espresso
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the hotel served in a shaded pavilion near Banteay Srei — smoked chicken sandwiches, fresh salads, tropical fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant Siem Reap or equivalent — contemporary Cambodian cuisine: grilled tiger prawns, slow-cooked pork ribs in palm sugar, and coconut panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon availability depends on wind conditions — confirm the evening prior. Banteay Srei is approximately 25 km from central Siem Reap; private vehicle required. The Landmine Museum visit is voluntary but highly recommended for cultural understanding.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Koh Ker — an ancient 10th-century capital with a dramatic seven-tiered pyramid temple (Prasat Thom) rising above the jungle canopy. Private vehicle and specialist guide for the 2-hour drive. Explore this rarely visited UNESCO-listed site in near-solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Beng Mealea — a sprawling, largely unrestored jungle temple that feels like a true archaeological discovery. Wooden walkways guide you through collapsed galleries draped in moss and roots. Return to hotel by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Spa evening at the hotel's luxury wellness center — traditional Khmer massage using lemongrass and kaffir lime oils, followed by a herbal steam bath. Private in-villa dinner option or quiet dinner at the hotel restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast: full Cambodian and Western spread — rice congee, fried eggs, fresh baguette, tropical fruits, and strong Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch enjoyed at Koh Ker or Beng Mealea — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, chocolate truffles, and cold-brew coffee in a premium hamper
meals.dinner: In-villa private dining: five-course Khmer tasting menu served by a personal butler — including prawn bisque, beef lok lak, and palm sugar crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Koh Ker and Beng Mealea day trip covers approximately 200 km round trip — depart by 07:00. Roads are good quality in November. Bring sturdy footwear for Beng Mealea's uneven terrain. Spa appointments should be booked the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise boat tour on the Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Visit floating villages (Kompong Phluk or Mechrey) with a knowledgeable guide explaining the unique amphibious lifestyle of lake communities. November is ideal as water levels are high and the flooded forests are accessible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap. Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique — observe master craftspeople restoring ancient Khmer art forms including silk weaving, lacquerware, and stone carving. Premium shopping opportunity for authentic handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Private tuk-tuk tour of Siem Reap's Old French Quarter and local night market. Followed by dinner at a chef's table experience at one of Siem Reap's top fine dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast: eggs royale, smoked salmon, freshly baked pastries, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch at a premium Siem Reap restaurant: fresh Tonlé Sap fish dishes, green papaya salad, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Chef's table at Cuisine Wat Damnak or Haven Restaurant — intimate tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring hyperlocal Cambodian ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap boat tour should be arranged through the hotel for a private vessel. Wear light layers as it can be breezy on the water. Artisans Angkor purchases directly support local artisan communities — meaningful luxury shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Private flight or premium van transfer from Siem Reap to Sihanoukville (approximately 1 hour by air or 6 hours by road — fly recommended). Check-in at a luxury beach resort on Otres Beach or a private island resort (Song Saa Private Island or Alila Villas Koh Russey).
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the beach resort. Afternoon at leisure on the pristine white sand beach. Optional: private snorkeling excursion to nearby coral reefs with a marine biologist guide, exploring the rich biodiversity of the Gulf of Thailand.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the private beach or resort jetty. Romantic beachfront dinner under the stars with fresh seafood grilled to order.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel before departure: tropical fruits, yogurt, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at beach resort: freshly caught grilled lobster, coconut rice, and tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner: whole grilled barramundi, tiger prawns, Cambodian seafood curry, and coconut ice cream, with curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book flights between Siem Reap and Sihanoukville well in advance — limited daily services. Song Saa Private Island requires speedboat transfer. November sea conditions in the Gulf of Thailand are generally calm and ideal for water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Private island-hopping excursion by luxury speedboat to the Koh Rong Archipelago — visit Koh Rong Sanloem's Saracen Bay and secluded coves. Snorkeling, kayaking, and swimming in crystal-clear turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a beachside spa treatment — couple's massage in an overwater pavilion or beachfront cabana using locally sourced coconut and jasmine oils. Followed by leisure time at the infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner on a sandbar at low tide (arranged by resort) — white-linen table set on a disappearing sandbar surrounded by the sea, with a personal chef and sommelier. Truly once-in-a-lifetime dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast: eggs station, fresh tropical fruits, smoked fish, pastries, and freshly brewed Cambodian Mondulkiri coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch on Koh Rong Sanloem: grilled fresh catch of the day, papaya salad, and chilled coconut water served in the shell
meals.dinner: Sandbar private dinner: five-course seafood tasting menu — oysters, lobster bisque, grilled whole snapper, prawn risotto, and passion fruit soufflé with champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: Sandbar dinner must be booked at least 2 days in advance and is tide-dependent. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. Water shoes recommended for rocky cove areas. November offers excellent underwater visibility.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure on the beach — optional stand-up paddleboarding, kayaking, or simply relaxing in a private cabana with a good book. Alternatively, a guided sunrise yoga session on the beach led by the resort's wellness instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cultural half-day excursion to Sihanoukville town — visit the local fishing port to see the daily catch brought in, explore Wat Leu (a hilltop Buddhist temple with panoramic coastal views), and browse the local market with a guide for authentic Cambodian coastal culture.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell beach dinner at the resort's premium restaurant — reflecting on the journey with a curated Cambodian rum and cocktail tasting paired with a seafood and Khmer cuisine dinner. Live acoustic music performance by local musicians.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast: freshly baked croissants, smoked salmon, tropical fruit platters, eggs to order, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch: grilled tiger prawn skewers, fresh spring rolls, mango salad, and iced lemongrass tea
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant: Cambodian rum tasting flight, charcoal-grilled lobster, Khmer beef skewers, fragrant rice, and coconut tapioca dessert with live acoustic performance

day_by_day.notes: Pack bags this evening for an early departure the following morning. Confirm checkout time and airport transfer with the resort concierge. Request a packed breakfast for early morning if flight departs before the restaurant opens.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning final swim or beach walk at sunrise — a peaceful farewell to Cambodia's coastline. Enjoy a final breakfast at the resort before private luxury transfer to Sihanoukville Airport or Phnom Penh International Airport for onward flights.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before departure, a brief stopover in Phnom Penh — visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda for a final dose of Cambodian royal history and culture. Alternatively, premium airport lounge access for a comfortable pre-departure experience.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through ancient temples, jungle ruins, floating villages, and pristine tropical beaches.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or packed gourmet breakfast hamper for early departures: fresh pastries, tropical fruits, Cambodian iced coffee, and assorted sandwiches
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge dining or, if stopping in Phnom Penh, lunch at Topaz Restaurant — French-Cambodian fine dining near the Royal Palace
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Arrange airport transfer the evening prior. Duty-free shopping at Phnom Penh International Airport offers Cambodian rum, silk products, and Angkor-themed artisan gifts. Ensure all purchased artifacts comply with Cambodia's cultural heritage export regulations.
